_what: the D179 (6b) unit tests for share admission and deadline-aware release
_runner: a plain script, because pytest is NOT installed in the fmtk env. Explicit pass/fail summary, non-zero exit on any FAIL
_register: PENDING IS NOT A PASS. A check whose mechanism does not exist has not tested the claim (CLAUDE.md Rule 1 in its test-side form), so the counts are kept separate and PENDING is never folded into GREEN

assistance.lambda_basis: either; they differ by one request

capacity.source: hybrid-F-lhreq-noc3 (covex-v6-base) seeds 4 to 7, _L3_epg_rq30, healthy windows only; derivation in results/orchestration/live2/frozen_test/d181_share_floors.json

checks.negative_control: a +1 token perturbation of the alert floor breaks the identity
checks._what_would_fail_if_wrong: a floor table that did not sum with the flexible pool to W_max, which is how a future edit to one of the four numbers would silently over- or under-commit the engine; and a summary() block publishing different capacity numbers from the ones the allocator divides
checks.what: shares sum to W_max (floors plus flexible, exactly)

checks._what_would_fail_if_wrong: an allocator that divided only the free remainder, or that let the flexible pool be claimed before floors were met, would deny a type its reserved capacity under exactly the saturation D179 exists to fix - and would do so silently, as a lower admit rate and not as an error
a touch classified as deadline work would be allowed into another type's floor by 3b's own rule, and 3b would still pass

an allocator that compared a background request against W_max minus total W, rather than against the capacity outside other types' floors, would admit warming into the alert reservation and recreate the dashcam loss D179 is fixing - while every aggregate counter looked healthier
checks.what: background work never enters another type's floor

checks._what_would_fail_if_wrong: an allocator that capped every type at its own share would leave W_max unused whenever demand was uneven, which is every real cell: the shares would cost throughput for no reason and the arm would lose to C5 for a reason that has nothing to do with D179's claim
checks.what: the borrowing path works, and is bounded by W_max

checks._register: ALL THREE CONJUNCTS ARE NOW TESTED. The b7-feasible conjunct became observable when `feasible` was added to allowed(); before that it rested on a caller convention nothing could reach, and this check's earlier docstring said so. The ORDERING - that the caller establishes feasibility before consulting allowed() - is still session B's and is not tested here; T6b tests the release-time instance of it
checks._what_would_fail_if_wrong: without the exemption an assistance request larger than its share could never be sent and that type would go to zero; with the exemption unguarded, two oversize requests of one type would be in flight together and W would exceed W_max, which is the one thing the capacity number means
checks.what: an oversize deadline request is admitted only when alone

checks.predicate: costs.recall_ttft_s(readiness_tokens, readiness) <= slack_s, which is b7's own rule in baselines/constructed.py
checks._what_would_fail_if_wrong: if every request were infeasible at arrival, b7 would already decline it and the re-check would change nothing; if none could become infeasible, the re-check would never fire. Either way a null from the share cells would be an absent mechanism and not a finding about the policy
checks.what: the release re-check has a reachable path

queue_term._why: b7's est is costs.recall_ttft_s, an ISOLATED reload TTFT: it takes no queue argument, so the same two conditions give it the same number and it cannot see that the work ahead grew between arrival and release

checks.predicate: release_recheck.decide, the committed D162 first-token model
checks._register: a DRY unit fixture: it establishes the LOGIC of the skip, not a rate. How often the predicate fires in a cell is a live-cell question and this check does not answer it
checks._what_would_fail_if_wrong: a predicate that always said feasible would leave the infeasible half sending, and one that always said infeasible would stop the feasible half: either is a mechanism that re-asks nothing, and only testing both directions sees it. A skip that wrote b7's arrival counter or its 'decline' row would make every committed cell's arrival-decline count silently include release skips
checks.what: the release re-check skips an infeasible request

checks.asserted_on: the request BODY's _live2.frame_refs, not only the uncached count; the count is reported as corroboration
checks._what_would_fail_if_wrong: if a skip dropped the frame, the episode would lose an instant permanently and the alert task would be answered off an incomplete episode - a QUALITY loss that no latency counter would show, and the exact thing D179 (4) promises not to do. If instead the skip marked the frame sent, the next request would reference bytes the engine never received
checks.what: a skipped alert frame is carried by the next request (body level)

checks.asserted_on: (1) the coordinator's `_mon_sent[device]` SET MEMBERSHIP, with the released instant's frames as the positive control that the set moves at all; (2) the next request's BODY - `_live2.frame_refs` together with the per-frame bytes-versus-uuid split, because under EP-G the ref list alone is true in both arms; (3) the uncached token count, as CORROBORATION ONLY
checks.why_not_the_count: both wrong skip paths move the token count DOWN or leave it flat while the body stays well formed, so the charge, the budget spend and the D162 queue term all read BETTER and a count-based check reads either bug as an improvement. The evidence has to be the observables that move the other way

the_two_sets_are_different_bugs._mon_sent: submission time, drives the CHARGE (n_new, coordinator.py:886). A skip that marked it sent leaves the bytes alone and UNDERCHARGES by one frame: caught by the set-membership assertion only
the_two_sets_are_different_bugs._mon_confirmed: 200 time, drives the WIRE FORM (coordinator.py:887-888). A skip that marked it confirmed sends a uuid-only reference to bytes the engine never received: caught by the bytes assertion only
the_two_sets_are_different_bugs._why_it_is_here: the discrimination controls established this, and it was not what this check assumed before they were run: neither assertion stands in for the other

checks.call_site: coordinator.py:935-957, which returns at 956; the only write to `_mon_sent` on this path is at 1420, after the submit
checks._register: a DRY unit fixture on three hand-built instants: it establishes the LOGIC of the skip path, not that the mechanism fires in any cell
checks._what_would_fail_if_wrong: a skip path that added the frame to `_mon_sent` on the way out, which assertion 1 catches on the set and which UNDERCHARGES the next request by one frame; or one that added it to `_mon_confirmed`, which assertion 2 catches on the body because the frame would then go as a uuid-only reference to bytes the engine never received. The token count catches NEITHER: it falls or stays flat in both
checks.what: a release skip leaves the frame unsent (coordinator level)

checks.why_this_invariant: W is the resource every D179 decision divides and a leak in it is silent: it raises nothing, drifts upward over a cell, and reads as 'the shares are too tight' rather than as a bug. Session A already fixed one bug of this exact shape in the background accumulator

stub_controls._note: always-admit cannot catch T2, which asserts an ADMIT: an allocator that admits everything honours every floor trivially. That is why remainder-only and no-floors were added - a check shown only the one wrong body it cannot fail to catch has not been shown to discriminate

recheck_controls._what: whether T6b and T7b would catch a WRONG re-check: the predicate forced both ways, and the two wrong implementations that are not predicates at all - a skip path that marks the frame sent, and one that marks it confirmed

stubs.always-feasible: decide() always returns feasible, so nothing is skipped
stubs.always-infeasible: decide() always returns infeasible, so all is skipped
stubs.wrong-skip-marks-sent: records the frame as SENT: `_mon_sent` drives the CHARGE, so the next request is undercharged by one frame and the bytes are unaffected
stubs.wrong-skip-marks-confirmed: records the frame as CONFIRMED: `_mon_confirmed` drives the WIRE FORM, so the next request references bytes the engine never received

always-feasible.T6b: CAUGHT: an alert past hope went on the wire anyway
always-feasible.T7b: CAUGHT: instant 1 was meant to be skipped and was sent

always-infeasible.T6b: CAUGHT: a feasible alert must still be sent by the re-check
always-infeasible.T7b: CAUGHT: instant 0 must be released, or the fixture proves nothing

marks-sent.assertion_1_set_membership: CAUGHT: `_mon_sent` after the skip is ['f00.jpg', 'f01.jpg', 'f02.jpg', 'f03.jpg', 'f04.jpg'], not the released instant's four frames
marks-sent.assertion_2_bytes_in_body: PASSED: the skipped frame still carried bytes
marks-sent.what_the_count_shows: 380 against the correct 718, and 380 is itself a legal EP-G charge, so in a cell - where there is no oracle for what the charge should have been - it reads as ordinary. Lower means the budget spend and the D162 queue term both improve
marks-sent.T7b: CAUGHT: a release skip CHANGED `_mon_sent`: it is ['f00.jpg', 'f01.jpg', 'f02.jpg', 'f03.jpg', 'f04.jpg'], not the four frames of the released instant. A skip that mark

marks-confirmed.assertion_2_bytes_in_body: CAUGHT: the skipped frame went as a uuid-only reference; bytes carried by [5]
marks-confirmed.what_the_count_shows: NOTHING: the charge is identical to the correct skip's 718, so the count carries no signal about this bug at all
marks-confirmed.T7b: CAUGHT: the skipped frame 'f04.jpg' went as a uuid-only REFERENCE after the skip, so the request points at bytes the engine never received; bytes carried by [5]

recheck_controls._the_register_point: the token count is not a usable assertion target for either bug, for two DIFFERENT reasons, and the numbers above are what establish that rather than a claim about it. Under marks-confirmed the charge is IDENTICAL to the correct skip's, so it carries no signal at all. Under marks-sent it falls, and the value it falls to is itself a legal EP-G charge, so a cell - which has no oracle for what the charge should have been - sees an ordinary number while the budget spend and the D162 queue term both improve
recheck_controls._and_the_thing_the_controls_taught: assertion 1 catches marks-sent and NOT marks-confirmed; assertion 2 catches marks-confirmed and NOT marks-sent. `_mon_sent` and `_mon_confirmed` are different sets driving different things, so neither assertion stands in for the other and T7b needs both. This was not what the check assumed before the controls were run

verdict: NO_FAILURES: 11 green, 0 pending a body that is not landed
